paths.label: Judo
paths.core: actively secure contact and control the opponent's posture
paths.lowUse: a brief grip check that can be released before committing to a hold
paths.secondary: a bounded throw or pin follow-up
paths.weakness: contact, size leverage and exposure while maintaining a hold
paths.contrast: Judo initiates contact and owns a maintained hold; it does not wait for an incoming action to redirect.

paths.label: Aikido
paths.core: use an observed incoming attack or movement to redirect the attacker
paths.lowUse: a low-cost flow response that is unavailable without a committed incoming action
paths.weakness: patient opponents, feints and attacks that are not observed in time
paths.contrast: Aikido reacts to a legally observed commitment; it does not create a proactive capture.

paths.label: Karate
paths.core: chain unarmed strikes to interrupt defense and destabilize posture
paths.lowUse: a quick single body strike with little recovery commitment
paths.weakness: weapon reach, approach interception and interruption between strikes
paths.contrast: Karate accumulates disruption through connected strikes; it is not one heavy armor-breaking commitment.

paths.label: Staff
paths.core: control distance, posture and travel lanes with nonlethal staff pressure
paths.lowUse: a short checking sweep that preserves retreat and does not seek a finish
paths.secondary: a route-denial guard zone or measured push
paths.weakness: close entry inside the staff and deliberately limited finishing power
paths.contrast: Staff controls routes and spacing; it does not inherit spear thrust damage or interception reach.

paths.label: Dagger
paths.core: enter short range through a flank or opening and exploit a brief attack window
paths.lowUse: a quick short-reach probe that can disengage without spending the opening
paths.secondary: a flank entry followed by a bounded vital-window strike
paths.weakness: short reach and firm frontal defense
paths.contrast: Dagger creates or exploits a close positional opening; it does not require a sheathed preparation state.

paths.label: Draw sword
paths.core: prepare in a sheathed stance and commit that preparation to one decisive release
paths.lowUse: maintain or abandon a ready stance without receiving the decisive strike benefit
paths.secondary: a prepared draw release followed by explicit resheathing
paths.weakness: preparation disruption, a missed release and the time needed to prepare again
paths.contrast: Draw sword converts a prepared stance into one release; ordinary sword play sustains offense and defense without resheathing.

paths.label: Spear
paths.core: use explicit long reach and a linear thrust before the opponent enters
paths.lowUse: a direct long-reach thrust with ordinary recovery and no interception promise
paths.secondary: a timed approach interception on the thrust line
paths.weakness: close entry, lateral movement and confined terrain
paths.contrast: Spear converts reach into thrust and interception; it does not claim the staff's route-control role.

paths.label: Axe
paths.core: commit to a heavy strike that damages armor or posture on contact
paths.lowUse: a measured heavy cut that preserves enough recovery to remain usable
paths.secondary: an armor-breaking or posture-breaking committed blow
paths.weakness: slow startup, miss recovery and resource consumption
paths.contrast: Axe pays one large commitment for break pressure; it does not accumulate an unarmed combination.

zodiacs.label: Initiative
zodiacs.operation: begin the path action before the opponent establishes control
zodiacs.condition: at engagement start or immediately after returning to neutral
zodiacs.tactic: shorten preparation while preserving an exit
zodiacs.cost: reduced certainty when used after the opening has passed
zodiacs.counter: delay, spacing or a false start

zodiacs.label: Accumulation
zodiacs.operation: build and retain path-specific readiness over time
zodiacs.condition: after uninterrupted preparation or maintained contact
zodiacs.tactic: trade immediate output for retained readiness
zodiacs.cost: lost buildup when preparation or maintenance is broken

zodiacs.label: Pressure
zodiacs.condition: while the target is defending or losing posture
zodiacs.tactic: commit forward to deny a passive defense
zodiacs.cost: greater recovery and a clearer counter window
zodiacs.counter: evade the commitment or counter during recovery

zodiacs.label: Evasion
zodiacs.operation: leave danger while retaining the path's low-level option
zodiacs.condition: when an observed threat enters its effective window
zodiacs.tactic: change spacing instead of contesting the threat directly
zodiacs.cost: cedes ground and may abandon accumulated readiness
zodiacs.counter: deny the exit lane or delay the threat

zodiacs.label: Area
zodiacs.operation: extend the path effect to a bounded lane or nearby area
zodiacs.condition: when geometry permits the declared area
zodiacs.tactic: control space rather than focus one target line
zodiacs.cost: higher commitment and weaker focused effect
zodiacs.counter: leave the bounded area or use obstruction

zodiacs.label: Restraint
zodiacs.operation: maintain path-specific pressure that limits escape
zodiacs.condition: after the path has established valid contact or control
zodiacs.tactic: exchange immediate damage for finite maintained control
zodiacs.cost: upkeep, exposure and an explicit escape opportunity
zodiacs.counter: break contact, cleanse the control or exhaust upkeep

zodiacs.label: Mobility
zodiacs.operation: move with the path action and continue a legal pursuit
zodiacs.condition: while a traversable route and observed target remain
zodiacs.tactic: join movement and action without granting teleportation
zodiacs.cost: movement resource use and predictable pursuit direction
zodiacs.counter: obstacles, route changes or a prepared interception

zodiacs.label: Harmony
zodiacs.condition: after choosing a lower-output controlled action
zodiacs.tactic: preserve repeated use instead of maximizing one exchange
zodiacs.cost: lower immediate pressure and time spent stabilizing
zodiacs.counter: force a decisive exchange before stabilization

zodiacs.label: Adaptation
zodiacs.operation: switch between two declared path modes after observation
zodiacs.condition: after legally observing the opponent's current response
zodiacs.tactic: use a bounded branch instead of a hidden-information guess
zodiacs.cost: the switch consumes time or resources and can be baited
zodiacs.counter: feint the observed response or change after the switch

zodiacs.label: Observation
zodiacs.operation: improve a path action using delivered, legal observation
zodiacs.condition: after the relevant motion, posture or opening is observed
zodiacs.tactic: wait for evidence before committing the path action
zodiacs.cost: delayed action and failure against concealed or false cues
zodiacs.counter: conceal, vary or falsify the relevant cue

zodiacs.label: Protection
zodiacs.operation: answer a threat with path-specific defense and response
zodiacs.condition: when a valid observed threat reaches the response window
zodiacs.tactic: protect first and counter only if the response succeeds
zodiacs.cost: depends on the incoming threat and yields initiative when unused
zodiacs.counter: wait, feint or attack outside the response contract

zodiacs.label: Breakthrough
zodiacs.operation: spend a bounded resource or recovery window for a decisive path action
zodiacs.condition: when the declared finishing condition is met
zodiacs.tactic: accept a visible risk to overcome established resistance
zodiacs.cost: high consumption, long recovery and punishable failure
zodiacs.counter: survive, evade or invalidate the finishing condition
